sections.title: China–India cross-border payment corridor
text: The China–India payment corridor supports significant trade flows between two of Asia’s largest economies. Businesses operating across this corridor frequently execute international payments for manufacturing supply chains, electronics trade, industrial procurement, and global commercial operations.

The global cross-border digital payment solutions market is projected to reach approximately $96.77 billion by 2034 , expanding at a 19.8% CAGR from 2024. This growth is driven by demand for faster settlement, real-time payment infrastructure, and more efficient ways to move money across complex international corridors.
At the same time, China–India trade continues to exceed $145 billion annually , creating a high-volume corridor for B2B supplier payments.

sections.title: China to India cross-border payments
text: Key questions about sending business payments from China to India — CNY to INR settlement, compliance, and supplier flows.

faq.q: What is the best way to send money from China to India?
faq.a: Businesses typically require enterprise payment infrastructure that supports supplier payments, treasury flows, and compliant cross-border settlement rather than consumer remittance tools.

faq.q: How do businesses send payments from China to India?
faq.a: Payments generally involve currency conversion, regulatory coordination, and settlement across international banking systems, often supported by cross-border payment providers.

faq.q: What is the best way to pay suppliers in India from China?
faq.a: The best way to pay suppliers in India from China is through a compliant B2B cross-border payments platform, such as Payfuture, that streamlines CNY to INR conversion, ensures regulatory alignment with China's FX controls and India's RBI/FEMA rules, and delivers predictable settlement while cutting traditional bank fees compared to SWIFT wires. Unlike traditional methods like telegraphic transfers (T/T) or letters of credit — which often face 2–5 day delays, intermediary friction, and high costs (typically 4–6%) — specialized platforms leverage local rails for faster execution, automated compliance checks, and full visibility into supplier invoice settlements.

faq.q: What is involved in transferring money from China to India internationally?
faq.a: Payments typically involve converting Chinese Yuan (CNY) into Indian Rupee (INR), coordinating between financial institutions, and meeting regulatory requirements in both jurisdictions.

faq.q: How does CNY to INR conversion work?
faq.a: Currency conversion takes place through foreign exchange markets, forming part of the international settlement process for cross-border payments.

faq.q: What payments are commonly made across the China–India corridor?
faq.a: Payments commonly support supplier settlements, outsourcing services, manufacturing inputs, logistics, and broader international trade operations.
